mainTopic: Signs of kosher eggs: how far they can be trusted, and what the 'mixed egg is a שרץ egg' rule teaches
overview: The amud opens with the last words of an earlier ברייתא listing foods we may get from a non-Jew: 'fish embryos.' The גמרא then quotes a ברייתא giving signs of a kosher egg: one round end and one pointed end, with the white around the yolk. If eggs have their own signs, why rely on the seller? The answers that the eggs were cut, or beaten in a bowl, are rejected, because beaten eggs may not be bought from a non-Jew at all. רבי זירא then says the egg signs are not reliable by Torah law, and proves it from רב אסי's eight birds of doubtful status. So the ברייתא is re-read: bad signs alone prove an egg is non-kosher, but good signs count only when the seller names a kosher bird, since some crow eggs look like pigeon eggs. Next the גמרא asks why the ברייתא says a mixed egg is a שרץ egg. רב עוקבא בר חמא says it matters for טומאה, but רבינא objects that it may be a snake's egg, so רבא says it matters for מלקות if someone eats a formed embryo. The גמרא challenges רבא, since a formed embryo in a kosher egg should also bring מלקות, and starts quoting a ברייתא that continues on the next amud.

steps.title: End of the earlier list: fish embryos
steps.stepSummary: The closing words of the earlier ברייתא add fish eggs to its list.
steps.whatsHappening: These two words finish the list in the earlier ברייתא, which started before this section. The last item on that list is fish eggs.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This line adds no new argument. It only completes the earlier ברייתא. The discussion that follows asks about the eggs mentioned in that ברייתא.

keyTerms.meaning: Fish embryos, meaning the eggs (roe) found inside a fish

phrases.english: Fish embryos.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the earlier ברייתא from before this section.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Fish eggs are included in the earlier ברייתא's list.

steps.title: Eggs have their own kosher signs
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a ברייתא listing signs of kosher eggs. This suggests there is no need to rely on anyone's word.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught about eggs: these are the signs of eggs. An egg that narrows and is rounded, with one end round and one end pointed, is kosher. If both ends are round or both ends are pointed, it is not kosher. If the white is outside and the yolk inside, it is kosher. If the yolk is outside and the white inside, it is not kosher. If the yolk and white are mixed together, it is surely the egg of a שרץ.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא with clear physical signs for kosher eggs. The hidden question is: if we can just look at the egg, why did the earlier ברייתא need to rely on what the seller says?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא gives two kinds of tests: the outside shape (one round end and one pointed end) and the inside layout (white surrounding the yolk). Since anyone can check these, depending on a non-Jew's identification seems unnecessary. So quoting this ברייתא works as a challenge.

keyTerms.meaning: Signs that show whether an egg is kosher
A creeping creature, which is not kosher

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up חֶלְבּוֹן (the white) and חֶלְמוֹן (the yolk). The kosher egg has the חֶלְבּוֹן on the outside.

phrases.english: And it is taught regarding eggs:
These are the signs of eggs:
Any that narrows and is rounded,
one of its ends is rounded
and one of its ends is pointed — it is kosher,
if both of its ends are rounded
or both of its ends are pointed — they are not kosher.
White on the outside and yolk on the inside — kosher,
yolk on the outside and white on the inside — not kosher,
yolk and white mixed with each other —
it is known that it is the egg of a creeping creature.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the earlier ברייתא's need to rely on the seller about eggs.
steps.kashyaTarget: The earlier ברייתא that relies on a non-Jew's identification of eggs.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Eggs can be identified by their shape and by how the white and yolk sit. So relying on the seller seems unnecessary.

steps.title: The eggs were cut
steps.stepSummary: The earlier ברייתא is talking about cut eggs, whose shape can no longer be seen.
steps.simpleTranslation: No, it is needed for eggs that are cut.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the earlier ברייתא deals with eggs that have been cut. You can't see whether the ends are round or pointed anymore.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The shape test needs a whole egg. Once the egg is cut, that sign is gone, so the seller's word becomes useful.

keyTerms.meaning: It is only needed for... (narrowing the case)

phrases.english: No, it is necessary where they are cut.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge from the egg signs.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The earlier ברייתא seemed to speak of whole eggs, which can be checked by shape.
steps.terutzMaskana: It speaks of cut eggs, where the shape test can't be used.

steps.title: Then check the yolk and white
steps.stepSummary: Even if the eggs are cut, the inside test should still work.
steps.simpleTranslation: But let him check the yolk and the white!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the answer. A cut egg still shows whether the white is outside or the yolk is outside.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Cutting removes only the shape sign. The second sign from the ברייתא, the layout of the yolk and white, should still be visible. So we still shouldn't need the seller's word.

phrases.english: But let him check the yolk and white?

steps.kashyaTarget: The answer that the eggs were cut.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The inside sign still works on a cut egg.

steps.title: The eggs were beaten in a bowl
steps.stepSummary: The eggs were beaten together in a bowl, so neither sign can be seen.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is talking about eggs beaten together in a bowl.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the eggs were already beaten and mixed in a bowl. There is no shape and no layout left to check.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With beaten eggs, both signs from the ברייתא are gone. So the only way to know is to rely on what the seller says.

phrases.english: With eggs beaten in a bowl.

steps.terutzHavaAmina: Cut eggs still show the yolk and white.
steps.terutzMaskana: Beaten eggs show neither sign, so we need the seller's word.

steps.title: We may not buy beaten eggs from a non-Jew
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא forbids buying beaten eggs from a non-Jew, so the earlier ברייתא can't be about beaten eggs.
steps.simpleTranslation: But in a case like this, may we buy from them? Wasn't it taught: we may not sell the egg of a טריפה bird to a non-Jew unless it is beaten in a bowl. Therefore we may not buy beaten eggs in a bowl from them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the last answer. Another ברייתא says beaten eggs may not be bought from a non-Jew at all, so the earlier ברייתא can't be talking about them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A Jew may sell a טריפה egg to a non-Jew only once it is beaten. Then the non-Jew can't pass it off later as a whole kosher egg. Because of this, beaten eggs held by a non-Jew might be those very טריפה eggs, so a Jew may not buy them. That makes the answer in step 5 hard to accept. The גמרא's reply comes next.

keyTerms.meaning: A bird with a fatal injury or defect, which is forbidden to eat

steps.confusionAlert: Two words look alike here. טְרֵפָה means a forbidden, injured bird. טְרוּפָה means beaten or mixed. The ברייתא uses both in one line.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows the logic behind the rule: we may sell only what can't be misused later, and so we may not buy that same kind of item back.

phrases.english: But in a case like this, do we buy from them?
But isn't it taught:
One may not sell the egg of a טריפה bird to a non-Jew,
unless it is beaten in a bowl;
therefore one may not buy from them
eggs beaten in a bowl.

steps.kashyaTarget: The answer that the earlier ברייתא speaks of beaten eggs.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Beaten eggs may not be bought from a non-Jew at all, so the earlier ברייתא can't permit relying on him in that case.

steps.title: רבי זירא: egg signs are not reliable by Torah law
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא takes a new approach. The signs of a kosher egg are not reliable on a Torah level, so we still need the seller's word.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רבי זירא said: The signs are not from the Torah.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives up on the 'beaten eggs' answer that was knocked down in Step 6. רבי זירא offers a completely new answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question was this: why rely on a non-Jew's word when the ברייתא gives signs? רבי זירא answers that the signs alone are not trustworthy by Torah law. So the signs are not enough by themselves, and the seller's word is still needed.

keyTerms.meaning: Signs (here, the shape and inside of the egg)
Not from the Torah; not reliable on a Torah level

phrases.english: Rather, Rabbi Zeira said:
The signs are not from the Torah,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the rejected 'beaten eggs' answer with a new answer to the question from Step 2.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefines the legal weight of the signs
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The signs in the ברייתא are fully reliable, so a seller's word is never needed.
steps.terutzMaskana: The signs are not reliable by Torah law, so a seller's word is still required.

steps.title: Proof from רב אסי's eight doubtful birds
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא proves his point. If egg signs worked, רב אסי's eight doubtful birds could be settled by checking their eggs.
steps.simpleTranslation: For if you don't say so, then about רב אסי's statement that there are eight doubtful birds: let us check their eggs! Rather, learn from this that the signs are not from the Torah.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי זירא backs up his claim with a proof from a statement of רב אסי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב אסי said there are eight birds whose kosher status is in doubt. If egg signs were reliable, we would just check their eggs and end the doubt. Since the doubt stays, the signs must not be reliable by Torah law.

keyTerms.meaning: For if you don't say so
Doubtful cases (here, birds of doubtful status)
Learn from this; a conclusion is drawn

phrases.english: For if you do not say so,
that which Rav Asi said:
There are eight doubtful ones –
phrases.notes: He means eight kinds of birds whose kosher status is unsure.

phrases.english: let one check their eggs!
Rather, learn from it:
the signs are not from the Torah.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports רבי זירא's claim from Step 7.
steps.raayaObject: Egg signs are not reliable by Torah law.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רב אסי's statement that there are eight birds of doubtful status. Their doubt could not exist if egg signs worked.

steps.title: Then what are the signs in the ברייתא for?
steps.stepSummary: If the signs can't be relied on, the גמרא asks what practical law the ברייתא is teaching by listing them.
steps.simpleTranslation: But for what law does it teach them?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on רבי זירא. If the signs don't count, why does the ברייתא list them at all?
steps.deeperAnalysis: A ברייתא does not list signs for no reason. If the signs are useless on a Torah level, the ברייתא seems pointless. The גמרא needs to find a real purpose for them.

keyTerms.meaning: For what practical law? What does this teach us?
It teaches it (the ברייתא lists it)

phrases.english: But for what law does it teach it?
phrases.notes: 'It' is the ברייתא with the egg signs.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבי זירא's view by asking what purpose the ברייתא's signs then serve.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי זירא's claim that the signs are not reliable by Torah law
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the signs carry no weight, the ברייתא listing them would be pointless.

steps.title: Bad signs prove non-kosher; good signs need the seller's word
steps.stepSummary: Negative signs prove an egg is certainly non-kosher. Positive signs can be trusted only when the seller names a specific kosher bird. Without a named bird, you can't rely on them, because some crow eggs look like pigeon eggs.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is what it means. If both ends are round, or both ends are pointed, or the yolk is outside and the white inside, it is certainly non-kosher. If one end is pointed and one end round, with the white outside and the yolk inside, and he tells you it is from a certain bird that is kosher, rely on it. With no details, don't rely on it, because some crow eggs look like pigeon eggs.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains what the ברייתא's signs are really for. They work fully to say an egg is non-kosher. To say it is kosher, they work only together with the seller's word.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Bad signs alone are enough to forbid an egg. Good signs are not enough alone, since a crow's egg can look like a pigeon's egg. But if the seller names a kosher bird, and the egg's signs fit, we may rely on it. This fits רבי זירא: the signs are a helper, not full proof.

keyTerms.meaning: This is what it means; a re-reading of the source

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think the good signs are useless. They count, but only together with the seller saying which kosher bird the egg came from.
steps.whatToRemember: Bad signs alone forbid the egg. Good signs plus the seller naming a kosher bird permit it. Good signs alone are not enough.

phrases.english: This is what it is saying:
If both of its ends are rounded,
or both of its ends are pointed,
or the yolk is outside and the white is inside –
it is certainly non-kosher.

phrases.aramaic: רֵישֵׁיהּ חַד חַד, רֵישֵׁיהּ חַד כַּד,
phrases.english: If one end is pointed and one end is rounded,
and the white is outside and the yolk is inside,
and he tells you it is from such-and-such bird,
phrases.notes: 'He' is the non-Jew selling the eggs.

phrases.english: and that bird is kosher – rely on it.
With no details – do not rely on it,
because there are crow's eggs
that look like a pigeon's.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 9 by re-reading the ברייתא so that its signs have a real use.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The signs in the ברייתא are pointless if they are not reliable by Torah law.
steps.terutzMaskana: Bad signs alone forbid the egg. Good signs work only together with the seller naming a kosher bird.

steps.title: Why does the ברייתא say a mixed egg is a שרץ egg?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the ברייתא's line that an egg with the white and yolk mixed together is a שרץ egg. It asks what law this teaches.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Master said: If the white and yolk are mixed with each other, it is known to be a שרץ egg. For what law is this said?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns to another line in the same ברייתא and asks why it is needed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Whether the egg comes from a non-kosher bird or from a שרץ, it is forbidden either way. So what difference does it make to know it is a שרץ egg? The גמרא is looking for a practical law that depends on this.

phrases.english: The Master said:
If the white and yolk are mixed with each other –
it is known to be the egg of a creeping creature.
For what law?

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר מָר: חֶלְבּוֹן וְחֶלְמוֹן מְעוֹרָבִין זֶה בָּזֶה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to a different line in the same ברייתא.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What practical difference it makes that the egg is identified as a שרץ egg, since it is forbidden either way.

steps.title: רב עוקבא בר חמא: it matters for טומאה
steps.stepSummary: רב עוקבא בר חמא says the point is about טומאה. If a lentil-sized embryo formed inside and the egg was punctured, it makes things impure, like a dead שרץ.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב עוקבא בר חמא said: It comes to say that if tissue formed and it was punctured, at the size of a lentil, it imparts impurity.
steps.whatsHappening: רב עוקבא בר חמא answers the question with a law of טומאה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A dead שרץ the size of a lentil makes things impure. So if this egg is a שרץ egg and an embryo grew inside, the embryo counts as a dead שרץ. Once the egg is open and it can be touched, it gives off טומאה. A non-kosher bird's egg would not do this.

keyTerms.meaning: Tissue formed; an embryo developed inside

phrases.english: Rav Ukva bar Chama said:
It comes to say that if tissue formed in it
and it was punctured, at the size of a lentil – it imparts impurity.

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Knowing it is a שרץ egg matters for טומאה. A lentil-sized embryo inside imparts impurity once the egg is opened.

steps.title: רבינא: maybe it's a snake's egg
steps.stepSummary: רבינא objects. A mixed egg might be a snake's egg, and a snake does not make things impure, so the egg can't be said to impart טומאה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא challenged it: But maybe it is a snake's egg?
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא attacks רב עוקבא בר חמא's answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Not every creeping creature gives off טומאה. A snake also lays eggs with the white and yolk mixed, and a dead snake is not impure. So the mixed-egg sign can't prove that the egg imparts טומאה.

keyTerms.meaning: Challenged it; raised a strong objection

phrases.english: Ravina challenged it:
But perhaps it is a snake's egg?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב עוקבא בר חמא's answer in Step 12.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that a mixed egg imparts טומאה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The mixed-egg sign also fits a snake's egg, and a snake does not impart טומאה. So the sign can't prove impurity.

steps.title: רבא: it matters for מלקות if eaten
steps.stepSummary: רבא gives a different answer. The ברייתא teaches that if an embryo formed and someone ate it, he gets מלקות for eating a שרץ.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רבא said: If tissue formed and he ate it, he is lashed for it because of 'a creeping thing that creeps on the earth.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבא replaces the טומאה answer with a law about eating.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Snakes are not impure, but every creeping creature is forbidden to eat. So whether it is a snake or another שרץ, eating a formed embryo from this egg brings מלקות under the שרץ prohibition. רבינא's challenge does not touch this answer.

keyTerms.meaning: The Torah's ban on eating creeping creatures

steps.whatToRemember: A mixed egg is a שרץ egg. The practical law is that eating a formed embryo from it brings מלקות. It is not about טומאה, since it might be a snake's egg.

phrases.english: Rather, Rava said:
That if tissue formed and he ate it –
he is lashed for it
because of "a creeping thing that creeps upon the earth."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 11 in a new way that avoids רבינא's challenge in Step 13.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Shifts the practical law from טומאה to the ban on eating
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא's point is about טומאה.
steps.terutzMaskana: The point is about eating. A formed embryo from any שרץ egg, even a snake's, brings מלקות.

steps.title: Why only the egg of a non-kosher creature?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רבא. If the ברייתא is teaching about מלקות for eating a formed embryo, the same should be true even for the egg of a טהורה bird.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, why specifically the egg of a non-kosher creature? The same should hold even for a kosher one!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks רבא's answer from Step 14. If eating a formed embryo brings מלקות, that should apply to kosher birds' eggs too, so why does the ברייתא talk only about a טמאה creature's egg?
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא said the ברייתא's point is מלקות for eating a formed embryo. But an embryo that has formed is forbidden as a שרץ no matter what kind of bird laid the egg. So connecting this law to a טמאה creature's egg seems pointless, and that makes רבא's reading look weak.

keyTerms.meaning: If so: if we accept the last explanation
Why specifically? Why single out this case?

steps.confusionAlert: The גמרא is not saying a kosher bird's egg is a שרץ egg. Its point is only that once an embryo has formed, eating it would bring מלקות in a kosher egg too. That is why naming a טמאה egg seems unnecessary.

phrases.english: If so, why specifically the egg of a non-kosher one?
phrases.notes: "If so" points back to רבא's answer in Step 14, that you get מלקות for eating a formed embryo.

phrases.english: Even that of a kosher one as well!

steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's reading that the ברייתא teaches מלקות for eating a formed embryo in a mixed egg
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the law is about eating a formed embryo, it applies equally to kosher eggs. So the ברייתא should not have tied it to the egg of a טמאה creature.

steps.title: Source that an embryo in a kosher egg is also forbidden
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a ברייתא on the פסוק "כל השרץ השרץ על הארץ" to back up its challenge. The quote continues on the next amud.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it is taught in a ברייתא: "Every swarming thing that swarms upon the earth"…
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts quoting a ברייתא to prove that even a kosher bird's embryo brings מלקות. It is setting up the proof, and the rest of the ברייתא comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The challenge in Step 15 needs a source, and this ברייתא will supply one through a דרשה on the פסוק. If the ברייתא shows that the פסוק covers embryos from kosher eggs too, then רבא's reading has trouble explaining why the mixed-egg ברייתא mentions only a טמאה egg.

keyTerms.meaning: "Every swarming thing that swarms upon the earth": the פסוק forbidding שרצים
A creeping or swarming creature that is forbidden to eat

phrases.english: As it is taught: "Every swarming thing that swarms upon the earth" –
phrases.notes: ויקרא 11:41. The ברייתא's explanation of this פסוק continues on the next amud.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּתַנְיָא: כׇּל הַשֶּׁרֶץ הַשֹּׁרֵץ עַל הָאָרֶץ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a source to support the challenge in Step 15.
steps.raayaObject: That eating a formed embryo brings מלקות even from a kosher bird's egg
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא expounding the פסוק "כל השרץ השרץ על הארץ" (ויקרא 11:41)
